headline: Every house on your beach lane was re-read live tonight and every one is still active at the same price — and a new Shell Banks find joins the board at $539,000 on 1.29 acres, the most land of anything on the lane.

lanes.label: Nashville
lanes.criteria: Boutique showroom for AllSouth · Nashville → Franklin/Brentwood corridor · 4,000–10,000 sf · buy up to $3M or lease · conversion candidates (restaurants, banks, retail boxes) welcome

highlights: Renovated, move-in-ready — zoning explicitly permits 'showrooms and display spaces'
1.16-acre dual-parcel site with strong corridor visibility
Second parcel is income-producing self-storage with upside
Seller open to a 3-year leaseback
listings.fitNote: Best sub-$3M ownership play in the whole corridor — right size, showroom-permitted zoning, $250/sf in the fastest-growing housing market in Middle TN.

listings.leaseRate: Sale, lease, BTS, or ground lease
highlights: Freestanding former hibachi/sushi restaurant on 0.95 ac
80 parking spaces at a signalized intersection, pylon sign in place
33,651 vehicles/day; 110K people within 5 miles
Offered for sale, lease, build-to-suit, or ground lease
listings.fitNote: Textbook restaurant-to-showroom conversion — the open dining floor becomes the gallery and the commercial kitchen becomes a live-demo cooking suite. Trade-off: east side of town, not the affluent south corridor.

highlights: Marketed as an office/showroom building, updated 2017
Berry Hill — Nashville's design & showroom district
42% leased ($96,920 NOI) — income while you build out
Minutes from 8th Ave S and I-440
listings.fitNote: Cheapest in-range Berry Hill buy, already described as a showroom building — and the partial tenancy pays carry during conversion.

highlights: Listed subtype is literally 'Showroom' — renovated 2019, big open studio space
Drive-in grade-level door for appliance delivery
On-site parking, very walkable design-district block
Owner-occupier opportunity
listings.fitNote: Turnkey boutique-showroom character in the city's design district; the drive-in door solves appliance logistics. Smallest floorplate on the list.

highlights: Exterior loading dock + basement storage — rare here, ideal for inventory
Abundant on-site parking; under 1 mile to I-65/I-440
Two 2,686 sf floors, right next door to 2605 Westwood
listings.fitNote: Office-to-showroom conversion: open first floor becomes the gallery, dock handles deliveries, upstairs becomes design offices. Buy it WITH 2605 next door and you've built a Berry Hill compound.

highlights: Inside Franklin's Factory District — the Factory at Franklin next door pulls 2M visits/yr
Trade-area median household income $106.7K
Zoning explicitly permits retail/showroom use
Owner-user sale, no long-term leases in place — price on request
listings.fitNote: Industrial-chic conversion in Franklin's hottest adaptive-reuse pocket — the Factory proves the high-end retail draw. Price is the open question; Gene can chase it same-day.

listings.address: Meridian Cool Springs, 2000 Meridian Blvd Ste 110
highlights: 7,235 sf first-floor retail, available NOW
Upscale mixed-use center with 3 on-site hotels (544 rooms)
446 parking spaces; 275 ft of Carothers Pkwy frontage
15,000+ office workers within walking distance
listings.fitNote: Strongest lease fit on the board — right size, immediate availability, and exactly the affluent daytime + hotel traffic a high-end appliance showroom feeds on.

highlights: Fully built-out endcap in a Sprouts-anchored center
~32,000 vehicles/day on Murfreesboro Rd / Hwy 96
453 parking spaces; available Sept 1, 2026; 5–10 yr terms
listings.fitNote: Former paint store = near-zero conversion cost and a homeowner/trade-pro traffic pattern that already matches appliance buying. Best value lease in Franklin.

listings.address: McEwen Northside Block E, 4020 Aspen Grove Dr
highlights: 8,816 sf ground-floor spec suite in a brand-new 280,000 sf live-work-play development
Direct I-65 access, curated walkable retail
The premium address in Cool Springs
listings.fitNote: The flagship-image play — new Class A shell where AllSouth builds exactly the showroom it wants. Expect the highest rent in this set.

listings.address: The Crossings of Spring Hill, Crossings Blvd
highlights: Two in-range suites, each available within 30 days
Class A power center: Target, Kohl's, Ross, ULTA, HomeGoods
4,946 parking spaces; huge Columbia Pike frontage
listings.fitNote: Captures the new-construction homeowner wave with co-tenancy that already pulls the home-furnishing shopper. Less 'boutique' in feel than the Franklin options.

highlights: Up to 4,592 sf contiguous in the Maryland Farms pocket
One of the ONLY in-range availabilities inside Brentwood proper
15–20 min to both Nashville and Franklin
listings.fitNote: Barely clears the 4,000 sf floor and visibility is interior-circle, but it's essentially the only way to plant a flag in Brentwood right now.

highlights: Pre-leasing a to-be-built neighborhood center bordering Spring Hill
Cold-shell delivery — spec gas/electric for live kitchen displays from day one
Sits in the fastest rooftop-growth path in the corridor
listings.fitNote: A bet on the growth corridor rather than a move-in space — construction timeline risk, but the cheapest path to a purpose-built showroom near the June Lake boom.

highlights: 775-acre master-planned community at I-65/Buckner Rd
Adjacent to thousands of planned new rooftops
Largest suite (4,277 sf) clears your size floor — bigger than the ~3,900 sf June Lake space you saw before
listings.fitNote: Minimum viable footprint, 2027 delivery — but nothing in the corridor puts a showroom closer to active new-home construction buyers.

intel.area: 🎨 Berry Hill / 8th Ave S (Nashville's design district)
pros: The de facto design & showroom district — designers and renovation trade pros are already there
The ONLY submarket with multiple in-range purchases under $3M (three verified, $2.0–2.7M)
10–15 min to Belle Meade, Green Hills, 12South — the city's richest renovation clients
High-character buildings that photograph beautifully for a premium brand
cons: Steep price per sf ($356–521) for older Class B/C product
Tighter parking than suburban retail
Most in-range buildings need conversion capital
Lower drive-by traffic than pike/interstate retail

pros: Top-20 wealthiest county in America; Cool Springs is its retail center of gravity
Deepest lease inventory in the corridor — verified options $30–45/sf including in-range suites available NOW
Massive daytime population + hotel traffic
The Factory District offers a rare adaptive-reuse ownership angle
cons: For-sale product at your size under $3M is essentially NONEXISTENT — this is a lease market
Highest rents in the corridor at the premium addresses
Strict design/signage codes
25–35 min from Nashville in rush hour

pros: Highest household incomes in the corridor, dense executive-homeowner base
Maryland Farms pocket sits 15–20 min from both Nashville and Franklin
cons: Almost zero in-range inventory in either direction — zoning deliberately constrains commercial supply, so this won't improve
The one in-range lease has interior-parcel visibility

pros: Fastest new-construction housing growth in Middle Tennessee — the ideal appliance-buyer pipeline
Best value: the only verified showroom-zoned building purchase in the corridor at $250/sf
Target-anchored co-tenancy traffic available within 30 days
cons: 45–55 min from Nashville — far for a store that also wants urban designers
Trade area skews production-builder/mid-market vs. ultra-luxury
Much of the best space is proposed/2027 delivery

pros: Affluent, fast-growing bedroom community
New mixed-use bringing quality small-shop retail
cons: Effectively no qualifying inventory — leases top out near 3,500 sf
No retail gravity yet; customers still drive to Cool Springs

lanes.note: Sweep verified Jul 29, 2026 on live listing pages. The headline: the affluent south corridor (Franklin/Brentwood) is a LEASE market at your size — ownership under $3M concentrates in Berry Hill and Spring Hill. Freestanding restaurant/bank conversion product is scarce in the south corridor right now; the one strong verified restaurant conversion (former Sakura, Hermitage) sits east of town. EVENING PASS Jul 30, 5:45 PM CT — ⚠️ STATED PLAINLY FOR THE THIRD SWEEP RUNNING: the page-by-page re-verify DID NOT HAPPEN. LoopNet returned 403 Forbidden to every automated request tonight, exactly as it did this morning and last night — and Crexi's Nashville retail index returned 403 as well, so both scraper routes into this lane are now closed, not just one. Every listing below still carries its Jul 29 morning verification. Nothing was added, nothing was removed, and no price was changed: stale-but-labelled beats invented. ⭐ THIS IS NO LONGER A GLITCH, IT IS A STANDING GAP — three consecutive failed passes means this lane needs a different source, not another retry. If a specific building matters to a decision this week, ask Gene and he will pull it from the MLS/CoStar side directly.

lanes.label: Knoxville
lanes.criteria: Showroom/warehouse combo · West Knoxville, Turkey Creek, Farragut, Lenoir City · 4,000–10,000 sf · buy up to $3M or lease · conversion candidates welcome

highlights: The one you flagged — 6,000 sf freestanding at Turkey Creek
Restaurant bones: open floor, parking, huge retail gravity
Inquiry route already in hand
listings.fitNote: Your restaurant-to-showroom pattern at the metro's #1 retail address. Gene is tracking the lease timing with the contact you provided.

highlights: ~4,000 sf open warehouse (14' clear) + ~2,000 sf finished office, renovated 2024
3 garage doors + 1 dock-high door
13,000 cars/day on Hwy 321, large pole sign, 3 min to I-75/I-40
Hit the market Jul 27 — brand new listing
listings.fitNote: Near-perfect template at $166/sf: highway-visible front converts to showroom, real warehouse and doors in back, interstate access for delivery trucks. New to market two days ago — these move fast.

highlights: Freestanding full-service restaurant, renovated 2022
~170' of frontage, ~28,000 cars/day and climbing, pylon sign
49 parking spaces on 1.29 ac, flexible C-2 zoning
listings.fitNote: Exactly your proven restaurant-to-showroom pattern — modern building, huge visibility, parking done. No dock, so warehouse stays light or off-site.

highlights: 8,500 sf single-tenant 2005 build — one of the newest in the corridor
150' of Central St frontage + 30 parking spaces (rare near downtown)
Walking distance to the new stadium district
Current occupant relocating — not a distressed closure
listings.fitNote: Design-forward downtown showroom in Knoxville's hottest urban-infill corridor; warehouse function would live off-site.

highlights: Brand-new flex: glass storefront entries in front, docks and drive-ins in back
26' eave heights; 5,000–42,500 sf shell — size it exactly to spec
Available now, tenant signage
listings.fitNote: The cleanest way to get a purpose-built showroom+warehouse without buying: glass front, dock rear, $13/sf.

highlights: 56,000 cars/day and 206' of frontage with monument sign
Eight 10'×10' roll-up doors, 23' ceiling in the 3,500 sf bay
~2,300 sf front section ready for showroom build-out
Move-in ready now
listings.fitNote: Auto-service-to-showroom conversion with exactly the right bones — retail front on a monster-traffic road, tall roll-up bay in back that swallows inventory. Lifts out, racking in.

highlights: Full build-out suites on Farragut's main artery, available now
1,380' of Kingston Pike frontage, 805 parking spaces
Highest-income trade area in the metro
Rear service access typical of the format
listings.fitNote: Flagship-showroom conversion on the pike where the metro's richest homeowners drive daily — keep bulk inventory in a cheaper flex lease nearby.

highlights: 6,900 sf outparcel at a brand-new 2026 center, partial build-out
Signalized intersection, across from the Hardin Valley school cluster
Knoxville's fastest-growing new-home submarket
listings.fitNote: The builders and homeowners buying $15K appliance packages drive past this corner daily; rear warehouse is modest, so pair with cheap storage.

highlights: Climate-controlled open warehouse/flex with its own loading dock
Freestanding, renovated 2022, fully fenced with lay-down yard
Minutes from Turkey Creek and Pellissippi Pkwy
24-hour access; janitorial included
listings.fitNote: Best-value west-side lease — a working showroom-warehouse near the money while you shop for a purchase.

highlights: 18 twelve-foot drive-in doors across two buildings
Fully renovated 2026: LED, paint, fixtures, gated 1.85-ac yard
Reception + 3 private offices in front
listings.fitNote: Turnkey warehouse-heavy option in fast-growing Powell — the reception front converts to a compact showroom, and loading is trivial.

highlights: First-floor flex suite off I-40/Pellissippi (an 11,609 sf suite also open)
15' unfinished ceilings, campus renovated 2010
Massive parking (97 surface + 602 covered)
listings.fitNote: Polished West Knox design-center-style option near the affluent base — Gene would confirm loading access before shortlisting.

highlights: 16–17' warehouse ceilings, 2 grade-level doors + mezzanine
3 finished offices, 2 covered exterior bays
Fully fenced 1.96 ac, two gated entrances
listings.fitNote: Cheapest real flex buy on the board ($191/sf) — works as the delivery/distribution hub paired with a showroom elsewhere; retail visibility is the trade-off.

highlights: 6,050 sf flex building + 2,480 sf warehouse building on 1.28 ac
Dock door + two drive-ins, 18' and 14' clear-span
Under 4 miles to downtown, off I-275
Listed Jul 15
listings.fitNote: Whole-campus lease with real doors at $13 NNN — strong ops/warehouse fit; it's an industrial pocket, not retail frontage.

pros: The metro's dominant retail gravity — pulls affluent shoppers from a 60+ mile radius
Direct I-40/I-75 access for deliveries
Dense $500K+ household concentration in the surrounding corridors
cons: Most expensive dirt and rents in the metro; flex product with docks is nearly nonexistent inside the retail core
For-sale inventory under $3M is extremely thin — owners lease, they don't sell

pros: Highest household incomes in the metro; heavy custom-builder activity feeding appliance demand
Kingston Pike delivers 30–40K cars/day past established centers
Strict sign ordinance keeps the corridor upscale — good brand adjacency
cons: Those same strict rules slow conversions and limit truck-court changes
Virtually no warehouse zoning — back-of-house must be light or elsewhere

pros: I-40/I-75 junction — best pure logistics access in the metro
Dramatically cheaper: ~$165/sf vs $250–500+ in West Knox
Feeds the booming Tellico Village lake-home market — an underserved high-end buyer pool
cons: Thinner retail traffic and less prestige than Turkey Creek, 15–20 min from the core
Smaller daytime population

pros: Happy Holler / stadium district is the metro's hottest urban-infill story — strong for a design-forward brand
Cheapest functional warehouse product with interstate access
Central drive-time position serves both sides of town for delivery routing
cons: The affluent homeowners live in the western suburbs, not here
Older stock — expect capex on roofs, HVAC, docks

lanes.note: Sweep verified Jul 29, 2026 on live listing pages. Showroom+warehouse combo product is genuinely scarce here — only 9 flex properties for sale metro-wide, and the good ones move fast (the Hwy 321 building listed Jul 27). The realistic playbook: buy function over address (Lenoir City/Powell at $145–245/sf) and lease a west-side showroom — or lease Amherst's new glass-front/dock-rear construction at $13/sf and skip the purchase. Side note: 120 Interchange Park Dr in Lenoir City also shows a separate $1.3M, 4,255 sf leased retail building on LoopNet — distinct from the lot you already know. LoopNet returned 403 Forbidden to every automated request tonight, and Crexi's index pages returned 403 too, so both routes into this lane are closed. Every listing below carries its Jul 29 morning verification. Nothing added, nothing removed, no price changed — stale-but-labelled beats invented. ⭐ Three consecutive failed passes is a standing gap, not a glitch: this lane needs a different source. lanes.label: Beach STR
lanes.criteria: Short-term-rental HOUSES (no condos) · Pensacola FL → Dauphin Island AL · up to $600K · 3+ bedrooms · water view/access ranked first · rental-proven properties badged

highlights: The one you flagged — unencumbered view East
Was listed $649K, now showing OFF MARKET
4BR/3BA, 1,656 sf raised construction
listings.fitNote: Gene is running this down with the listing side — if it's withdrawn rather than under contract, there may be an off-market opening.

highlights: Page now reads REDUCED $20K and "MOTIVATED SELLER - BRING AN OFFER" (verified Jul 30) — asking held at $375,000
Separate cottage/flex structure + 2-car garage
New roof and gutters, move-in ready
Deeded boat-launch access
~5 min to Johnson's Beach / Perdido Key
listings.fitNote: The yield standout of this sweep: a $52–65K gross projection on a $375K basis, in STR-friendly unincorporated Escambia County.
listings.strNote: Needs FL vacation-rental license + county tourist tax registration — straightforward, no city ban here.

listings.rentalHistory: Listing states: "Currently generating $3,600+ per month in rental income"; approved for both short-term and long-term rental
highlights: Only property on this lane with rental income stated ON the listing — $3,600+/mo, verified Jul 30
Bay views + community pool over the bay
2021 build, private primary balcony
Golf-cart ride to The Wharf / Margaritaville

highlights: Heated private pool + connected back deck
Turn-key: furnishings and golf cart convey
2025-updated primary bath, hurricane hardware
Two under-home storage areas
listings.fitNote: Heated pool + golf cart is the highest-converting amenity combo on the island — day-one STR with zero setup capex. ⚠️ LINK NOTE (Jul 30): the listing broker's property page now returns 404, but the listing itself re-verified ACTIVE at $575,000 / 3BR / 2BA / 1,512 sf on independent sources this morning — so this is a broken link, not a dead listing. Direct link is being re-sourced; ask Gene for the MLS sheet in the meantime.

highlights: Raised cottage, Gulf views from big covered deck
Gulf side of the island — steps to sand
Recent roof, HVAC, windows, appliances
Under-house entertaining + gear storage
listings.fitNote: Gulf-side view cottage under $550K is the island's classic STR play, sitting in the beach-demand zone that books best.

highlights: Deeded Little Lagoon access
3 FULL baths — rare at this size and price
West Beach / lagoon neighborhood
Cut $60K from original $645K list
listings.fitNote: 7+ months on market and a $60K cut = negotiation room; three full baths supports an 8-sleeper setup near the beach zone.

highlights: Water views from every window — Little Lagoon
Beach access within a quarter mile
Full reno: quartz kitchen, new electrical/plumbing
0.32-ac wooded lot, never hurricane-damaged
listings.fitNote: Lagoon view plus a quarter-mile beach walk in the West Beach corridor — prime STR positioning under $550K.
listings.strNote: This stretch generally falls inside Gulf Shores' permitted STR district — we verify the parcel before any offer.

highlights: Sold fully furnished — seamless STR start
Elevated 2005 build, new 5-ton HVAC + metal roof
Double corner lot (0.34 ac), fully fenced
Nearly 2,000 sf — sleeps a big group
listings.fitNote: Biggest livable square footage under $500K on the island; fresh mechanicals keep insurance and setup friction low.

highlights: Fortified roof (3 yrs) + custom window shields
Cargo lift — guests love it
Only house on a quiet street, beach paths near
Mature citrus and fruit trees
listings.fitNote: Privacy plus fortified construction makes a durable, low-cost-to-run STR — pitch it on quiet-island seclusion.

highlights: 2026 Gold Fortified NEW construction
Impact-rated windows/doors, elevated
Quartz kitchen, 10-ft ceilings
Marketed for vacation/investment use
listings.fitNote: Gold Fortified certification materially cuts wind insurance — the biggest STR expense line on the island — and new-build photos rent well.

highlights: 68 ft of canal frontage + private boat ramp
West Beach side, short hop to the Gulf
Elevated on pilings, metal roof
Updated kitchen, bath, flooring
listings.fitNote: Fish-from-the-deck canal frontage inside the beach-zone STR district — a distinct boat-crowd niche vs. commodity beach boxes.

highlights: SIX bedrooms — huge sleeps count for the price
Minutes from Perdido Key beaches
Water-oriented community (fishing/kayaking)
Only 2 baths — budget to add one
listings.fitNote: Sleeps-12 potential at $430K with no city license needed; adding a third bath would materially lift nightly rate and reviews.

listings.rentalHistory: Listing markets the separate living quarters as a rental opportunity
highlights: True dual-unit: two kitchens, separate entrances
Rent both units, or live-in-one/rent-one
Walk to Lighthouse Bakery and town core
2021 HVAC, fenced yard, two storage rooms
listings.fitNote: Cheapest door-count play on the board — two rental units under one roof at $359K.
listings.strNote: We'd confirm the town STR license covers both units and check minimum-stay overlay rules for the parcel.

listings.city: Gulf Shores (Laguna Park / Fort Morgan Rd)
highlights: Water view of Little Lagoon — the lagoon side is where Gulf Shores value lives, per this lane's own read
2,129 sf / 3BR / 3BA on the Fort Morgan Rd corridor
Detached house, not a condo — meets the hard rule on this lane
listings.fitNote: NEW Jul 30. The one find this morning that clears every gate on this lane at once: detached, 3BR+, under $600K, and an actual stated water position rather than water-adjacent. At $282/sf it is better value per foot than most of the Dauphin Island set. ⚠️ NO rental income or projection is stated on the listing, so none is claimed here — and Fort Morgan Rd corridor STR rules vary parcel to parcel, so the zoning check matters more here than usual.
listings.strNote: ⚠️ STR eligibility NOT stated on the listing — parcel-level check required before any offer.
listings.broker: Sourced via CondoInvestment MLS feed (Gulf Shores homes $500–600K), verified Jul 30, 2026

highlights: 1.29-ACRE lot — roughly 4x the land of anything else on this lane
2,242 sf, 3BR / 2BA
Shell Banks, on the Fort Morgan Rd corridor between town and the peninsula
Listed by Engel & Völkers Gulf Shores
listings.fitNote: The LAND play on this lane rather than the water play. At 1.29 acres it is the only listing here with real room — parking for a crowd, a pool, an outbuilding or a future second structure are all on the table, which is exactly what a rental with turnover needs and what the quarter-acre island lots cannot offer. Fort Morgan Rd draws from both the town and the peninsula rental markets.

Loyal repeat-guest 'Sunset Capital' brand

Lower nightly-rate ceiling and shorter season than Gulf Shores/Orange Beach

Best demand engine on the AL coast — Hangout Fest, sports tourism, national brand
Lagoon/canal waterfront under $550K — waterfront STR product you can't touch gulf-front
cons: STR district rules bar new rentals in most neighborhoods north of the beach area — parcel-level verification is mandatory

City license, inspections, and 13%+ lodging tax compress margins

Quiet beaches, week-long family bookings, high repeat rates
Gold Fortified new builds along Hwy 180 cut insurance meaningfully
cons: Fee-simple houses under $600K nearly extinct on the peninsula proper — budget buys the lagoon side
20–40 min to restaurants/groceries — reviews penalize the drive
Highest wind/flood exposure on the AL coast at the tip

Florida insurance is the most stressed on this coast — quotes before offers

lanes.note: Sweep verified July 2026 across MLS-fed broker sites. Before any offer: parcel-level STR zoning check + current wind/flood quotes — insurance swings net yield more than nightly rate in every one of these markets.
